about:
# DandersFrames

A party and raid frame addon for World of Warcraft: Midnight.

## Features

- Customizable party and raid frames
- Aura tracking and dispel indicators
- Private aura support
- Buff/debuff indicators with targeted spell tracking
- Range checking and highlight options
- Flat raid frame styling
- Pinned frames and flexible sorting (including secure sort)
- Import/export profile support
- Built-in test mode for configuration
- Minimap button via LibDBIcon

## Installation

1. Download the latest release from the Releases page
2. Extract the `DandersFrames` folder into your `World of Warcraft/_retail_/Interface/AddOns/` directory
3. Restart WoW or type `/reload` in-game

## Contributing

Pull requests are welcome! If you'd like to contribute, please follow these steps:

1. Fork this repository
2. Create a feature branch (`git checkout -b my-feature`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m "Add my feature"`)
4. Push to your fork (`git push origin my-feature`)
5. Open a Pull Request with a clear description of your changes

Please test all changes thoroughly in-game before submitting.

All pull requests are reviewed at our discretion, and not all submissions will be merged. We appreciate every contribution, but we reserve the right to decline changes that don't align with the direction of the project. We encourage respectful and constructive collaboration, and we're grateful to everyone who takes the time to contribute.

## Libraries

This addon bundles the following third-party libraries, each under their own respective licenses:

- LibStub
- CallbackHandler-1.0
- AceSerializer-3.0
- LibDataBroker-1.1
- LibDBIcon-1.0
- LibDeflate
- LibSerialize
- LibSharedMedia-3.0

## Development setup

This repo is a **container**, not an addon folder. Its root holds two addon
folders rather than being one:

```
<repo>/
  DandersFrames/            the addon (always loaded)
  DandersFrames_Options/    settings panel, designers, debug tools
                            (## LoadOnDemand — loads when /df is opened)
  README.md  CHANGELOG.md  .pkgmeta  .github/  Tools/  docs/
```

WoW only loads addons from `Interface/AddOns/<Name>/<Name>.toc`, so the repo
cannot live inside `AddOns/` any more, and a load-on-demand companion has to be
a **sibling** top-level folder rather than a subfolder. Clone the repo anywhere
and link **both** folders in with **directory junctions** — junctions (`/J`),
not symlinks (`/D`), so no admin rights or Developer Mode are needed.

### One-time, per game install

From your `Interface/AddOns` folder, with WoW closed:

```
mklink /J "DandersFrames"         "C:\path\to\repo\DandersFrames"
mklink /J "DandersFrames_Options" "C:\path\to\repo\DandersFrames_Options"
```

A junction cannot replace an existing directory, so anything already at those
names has to go first. Repeat per game install — `_retail_`, `_ptr_`, `_beta_`
— so six junctions if you run all three.

> ### ☠ Removing an existing `AddOns/DandersFrames` — read this
>
> If you already develop DandersFrames, that path is **probably a junction, not
> a folder**, and `rm -rf` in Git Bash *follows it* and deletes your working
> tree on the other side. Losing an unpushed branch to a cleanup step is a
> miserable way to start.
>
> Check what it is, then remove it as a link:
>
> ```
> cmd //c dir /AL "DandersFrames"     # lists it if it is a junction
> cmd //c rmdir "DandersFrames"       # removes the LINK, never the target
> ```
>
> `rmdir` refuses to touch a non-empty real directory, so it fails safe either
> way. Only reach for a recursive delete once you have confirmed it is a real
> folder you actually want gone.

**If `/df` does not open after this**, the usual cause is only the first
junction existing — the panel lives in `DandersFrames_Options`, so the addon
loads fine and the settings command does nothing useful. Note also that a new
addon folder is only picked up on a **full client restart**, not `/reload`.

After that, edit in the repo and `/reload` in game; the junction means there
is no copy or sync step. `git status`, branches and PRs are unchanged — one
repo, one branch, one PR.

### Why a container, rather than one addon folder

`DandersFrames_Options` is a load-on-demand companion holding the settings
panel, both designers, the click-casting UI, test mode and the debug tools —
30 files, about a third of the code. WoW resolves `LoadAddOn("Name")` to
`AddOns/Name/Name.toc`, so a companion has to be a top-level addon folder — a
sibling of `DandersFrames`, not a subfolder. That is only possible if the repo
root is a container, hence this layout.

Measured on the PTR build: with that payload not loaded, DandersFrames uses
**8,957 KB instead of 12,348 KB — 3,391 KB less, 27.5%** — and ~55,000 lines
are never parsed at login. The saving lasts until the settings panel is
opened; the login cost is avoided every time.

Users do none of this: the packager ships the two folders as siblings in the
zip, and `.pkgmeta` maps them. The junctions exist only because there is no
packager running locally.

**Nothing may depend on the companion to work.** Live behaviour that happened
to live in a settings file has to move back to the main addon, not be guarded
away — the auto-profile engine, the click-casting bootstrap and the aura
migrations are all resident for that reason.

The rule in practice, when adding anything:

| Kind | Do |
|---|---|
| Deliberate user action (`/df test`, unlock, profiler, selective import/export) | **Load** the companion — `DF:EnsureOptionsLoaded()` |
| Background event (a talent-change UI refresh) | **Guard** and no-op — a refresh with no UI is correctly nothing |
| Live behaviour | **Keep it resident** |

☠ A companion file's `...` is the *companion's* addon table, not ours. Every
file there binds `local DF = DandersFrames` — the global published at
`DandersFrames/Core.lua:9`, **not** by `## AllowAddOnTableAccess`, which
governs private-table access and is unrelated to the global name.

### Verification tooling

A set of checkers was written during the restructure — TOC completeness, load
order, split-plumbing aliases, the load-on-demand boundary, and login-time work
stranded in the companion. Two are worth running after anything that moves code
between files: the alias checker (this caught two in-game crashes) and the
boundary checker (which watches the `DF`, `GUI` and `CC` namespaces separately,
because one that watches a single namespace is blind to the others).

⚠ These live under `docs/reorg-tools/`, which is **gitignored and not part of
this repo** — ask Krathe for a copy. Most of `docs/` is local; the one tracked
exception is `docs/gui-conventions.md`. Some in-code comments cite
`docs/reorg-tools/splits.manifest` for the same reason.

## [6.1.0]

### New Features

- (Fading) New **Show Below Threshold Through Frame Fade** option in **Health Threshold Fading**. Below the threshold a frame ignores Frame Fade, so you can hide healthy frames out of combat and still see anyone who is hurt. Try Frame Fade at 0% out of combat and 100% in combat with this on.
- (Fading) WoW Forever: new **Show When Pet Is Not Happy** option in **Frame Fade**. Your pet's frame shows through Frame Fade while your pet is Content or Unhappy, in or out of combat.

- (Pet Frames) WoW Forever: your hunter pet's happiness now shows as a face beside the unit frames pet frame and your own party/raid pet frame. Hover it for damage, loyalty, diet, training points and experience; a small arrow warns when loyalty is dropping. The pet frame's border, name and health bar can also be colored by happiness (colors under **Display > Colors**), and the pet's **Text Designer** has a **Pet Happiness** category. Settings are on the pet's **Unit Icons** page and **Display > Pet Frames**.

- (Click-Casting) Choose exactly which frames each binding works on: party and raid separately, each unit frame (player, target, target of target, focus, focus target, pet, boss) on its own, and Other Frames. One button can now do different things on different frames, like targeting on the target frame and healing on your party. Set it under **Apply to Frames** when you edit a binding; your existing bindings keep working everywhere they did.

### Improvements

- (Modules) Modules now use on/off switches instead of checkboxes, so it's clearer what's on.
- (Modules) Each unit frame (player, target, focus, pet, boss) has its own on/off switch on the Modules page.
- (Modules) The Unit Frames and Party/Raid lists on the Modules page can be folded away.
- (Unit Frames) Added tooltips to settings that weren't self-explanatory, like Frame Source and Kick-Ready Mark.
- (Settings) Added tooltips to many settings that weren't clear from their name alone, across raid layout, sorting, pinned frames, aura bars, targeted spells, fading, tooltips, highlights, icons, absorbs, heal prediction and health bars.
- (Resource Bar) With **Placement** Below or Above a horizontal health bar (or Left of / Right of a vertical one), the health bar keeps its full size and the resource bar is cut out of it, so a see-through frame border tints the health bar the same on every side. A bar at the end the health bar fills from or towards still shrinks the health bar, so the whole health range stays readable. (by Krathe)
- (Fading) **Frame Fade** has moved from the **Frame** page to the **Fading** page, for party, raid and every unit frame. Your settings are unchanged. Linked unit frames now share Frame Fade through the **Fading** link instead of **Frame**.
- (Fading) **Frame Fade** and Health Threshold Fading's above-threshold opacity can now go down to 0% to hide a frame completely. A hidden frame can still be clicked and click-cast.
- (Fading) Status icons (summon, AFK, phased, raid role, ping and the rest) now fade along with **Frame Fade** instead of staying bright on a faded frame.
- (Unit Frames) The **Visibility** page can now show a frame only in a **Party** or only in a **Raid**, and show or hide it while **Resting** in an inn or city.
- (Fading) **Show In-Combat Fade When Hovering** now works without **Separate Combat Fade**: hovering a faded frame shows it at full opacity.
- (Settings) The search box at the top of the side menu now filters in place: the menu shows only pages with a matching setting, and each page shows only the matching settings. Clear the box to see everything again. The search on **Home** lists results from every module, and clicking one takes you straight to that setting.
- (Settings) Search understands related words and small typos. Try "transparency" or "opacity" to find fade and alpha settings, or "hide" to find visibility options. Partial words work as you type.

### Bug Fixes

- (Unit Frames) Fix raid buffs such as Fortitude never showing on the buff bar, even with All Buffs on.
- (Fading) Fix a frame with a dispellable debuff dropping back to fully faded instead of showing.
- (Fading) Fix the health fade briefly resetting with Element-Specific Alpha on.

## [6.0.0]

### New Features

- (Unit Frames) New **Unit Frames** module: player, target, target of target, focus, focus target, pet and boss frames, with the same depth of settings as your party and raid frames. It starts switched off: say yes to the popup, or turn it on from the **Modules** page, then find each frame's settings under **Units** in the icon bar. This is an early version, so please report anything odd.
- (Unit Frames) Draw each frame as bars or as **rings** round a round portrait, with up to 8 rings for health, power, class power, shields, heal absorbs and heal prediction. Find it on a frame's **Frame Style** page.
- (Unit Frames) Each frame has its own Text Designer template, and Player and Pet have their own Aura Designer. Link frames on the **Linked Frames** page so changing one changes the other, preview everything with the **Units** test mode, and copy a page's settings from another frame or from your party and raid frames.
- (Settings) New settings layout: an icon bar down the left side replaces the Global / Party / Raid / Binds tabs. **Groups** holds your party and raid settings, **Binds** is click-casting, and **Modules**, **Profiles** and **Global** sit at the bottom.
- (Settings) New **Home** page: search every setting, jump to any part of the addon, see what's new, and get a short **Needs attention** list with one-click fixes, such as Blizzard frames still showing or test mode left on.
- (Settings) New **Modules** page to turn Group Frames (Party and Raid separately), Click-Casting and Unit Frames on or off, or reset one to its defaults.
- (Profiles) Every profile tool now lives on the **Profiles** page: profiles, spec switching, Auto Layouts, click-casting profiles, import/export and changed settings. You can now **rename** profiles, and one import box accepts profile, click-casting and filter strings.
- (Pet Frames) Pet frames can now show buffs and debuffs. Set their size, count and position on the new **Buffs** and **Debuffs** cards of the **Pet Frames** page; what they show follows your main buff and debuff settings.
- (Aura Designer) New **Only on My Frame** option for indicators and effects: show a buff, or a "missing" reminder such as Inner Fire, only on your own frame.
- (Resource Bar) New **Placement** option: keep the bar on top of the health bar (as before), or put it **Below**, **Above**, **Left of** or **Right of** it. Along a side the health bar shrinks to make room, and the bar gets its own offsets and frame level. Turn off **Match Health Bar Width** for a shorter bar and use **Anchor** to place it. (by Krathe)
- (Frame) New **Keep Health Bar Inside Border** option on the Border card, so a see-through border sits over the frame background on every side. Off by default. (by Krathe)
- (Absorbs) New **Overflow** sliders for absorbs (Attached (overflows) mode) and heal prediction, so shields and incoming heals can run past the end of the health bar, up to a full bar's length. Off by default. (by Krathe)
- (Test Mode) The test popup is now a slim popout with a rail of modes. With Indicator Info on, click an element on a test frame to open its settings.
- (WoW Forever) Missing Buffs can now watch Divine Spirit, Thorns (tanks only by default), Blessing of Salvation (off by default) and one paladin blessing per role, on the new **Class Buffs (WoW Forever)** card.
- (Mover) An anchored element can mirror its target's position on X and Y.
- (Rested Indicator) New soft outer glow style.
- (Icons) Combat and leader icons use sharper art.
- (DandersMover) Frames anchored to another addon's frames now follow them automatically.
- (DandersMover) Adding DandersMover to an addon now takes far less code. Addon authors can pass `db` and `dbKey` in place of `getPos`, leave out `onChanged`, and let DandersMover place the frame and detect protected frames. See the Developer Guide.

### Improvements

- (Absorbs) Clearer names for the absorb and heal absorb Display Mode options, with a tooltip explaining each. Saved settings are unchanged. (by Krathe)
- (Performance) Debug logging now costs nothing while it is off. (by Krathe)
- (WoW Forever) Arcane Intellect and Divine Spirit no longer show as missing on warriors and rogues.

### Bug Fixes

- (Range) Fix enemy targets fading as out of range when a hunter is in melee range.
- (Profiles) The export name now defaults to your current profile's name instead of "My Profile".
- (Aura Designer) Group sliders and global text colours now update your frames while you drag them.
- (Pinned Frames) Fix pinned frames staying registered after leaving raid mode.
- (Search) Fix search staying stuck on "Indexing settings..." after combat.
- (Mover) Clicking now brings the mover controls back if they stayed faded after alt-tabbing.
- (Test Mode) Turning off Color by Time Remaining now takes effect on test frames.
- (Settings) Fix a large gap above Reduced Max Health and uneven resource colour swatches.
- (DandersMover) One addon with a broken mover registration can no longer stop the editor opening for everyone else.
- (DandersMover) Anchoring a frame to something that isn't on screen yet no longer makes it jump.
- (WoW Forever) Flasks, potions, elixirs, Spirit of Redemption, Camp Benefits and Prayer of Mending now show in aura filters, and shadow protection potions no longer count as the priest buff.

## [5.6.2]

### New Features

- (WoW Forever) Names on frames now show the full name by default. A new **Name Format** option for name text in the Text Designer lets you switch to the first name only, the first name with a last initial, or initials. Max Length still applies to the result, so raise it if full names get cut short.

### Bug Fixes

- (WoW Forever) Fix your own frame disappearing from party frames when using Self Position First/Last, Sort by Class, Separate Melee & Ranged DPS or Alphabetical sorting.

## [5.6.1]

### Bug Fixes

- (Text Designer) Text groups have their Items list back, so you can add, reorder, remove and customise the data a group shows again.

# DandersFrames Changelog

## [5.6.0]

### New Features

- (Bars) New **Tile** and **Texture Layers** options for bar textures: repeat a pattern along the bar and stack up to two extra pattern and shading layers, with presets and a live preview. Off by default. (by Krathe, original idea by Aphoex)
- (Bars) A **Mirror** option leans striped textures the other way. (by Krathe)
- (Bars) Twelve new pattern textures for Texture Layers. (art by Aphoex)

### Improvements

- (Performance) Smoother raids: no more multi-second freezes when joining a large group or switching auto layouts, no stutter on pull, and less work during combat. (by Krathe)
- (Auto Layouts) Joining a raid or switching layouts no longer flashes the wrong layout or rebuilds frames twice. (by Krathe)
- (Auras) Buffs, debuffs, the dispel overlay and Aura Designer indicators now set up and update during combat. (by Krathe)
- (Debuffs) Ticking both Non-Player and From Any Player now counts as All Debuffs, with one Max Debuffs limit. (by Krathe)
- (Tooltips) The in-combat and out-of-combat tooltip settings now follow whether you are in combat. (by Krathe)
- (Heal Prediction) Show Overheal now lights a spark at the end of the health bar, and absorbs and heals no longer draw outside the bar. (by Krathe)
- (Absorbs) The Attached absorb's Clamp Mode setting is removed; existing setups move to Missing Health. (by Krathe)

### Bug Fixes

- (Range) Range fading now checks all your range spells, so classes such as Evoker no longer fade players who are in range. Devourer Demon Hunters get their own range spells, and talent changes apply without a reload. (by Krathe)
- (Raid Frames) With a name-list sort, players who join mid-combat now appear as soon as combat ends. (by Krathe)
- (Reduced Max Health) The health bar no longer runs under the reduced max health area after a refresh. (by Krathe)
- (Fonts) Fonts are correct straight away after a reload in combat. (by Krathe)
- (Dispel) The dispel overlay and symbols now show in battlegrounds, arena and after logging in where auras are restricted. (by Krathe)
- (Icons) **Hide In Combat** status icons now hide as combat starts, not after it ends. (by Krathe)
- (Text Designer) Text that stopped updating mid-fight now catches up as soon as it's allowed again. (by Krathe)
- (Absorbs) No more stray heal prediction bars or absorb boxes flashing beside the frames when joining or leaving a group. (by Krathe)
- (Heal Prediction) Hidden on offline and dead players. (by Krathe)
- (Borders) Class and role coloured borders no longer get stuck on the plain colour after the raid reshuffles. (by Krathe)
